decision: Split rlsentry into a chain; first task is anon-probe (live black-box scan with anon key)
why: The request is a whole product; the black-box probe is what directly answers "verification, not reminders" and fixes the verdict/report model the rest builds on

decision: Write probe on by default but must never persist a row; uncertain → verdict unknown
why: Write exposure is half the CVE; scanning real prod data makes persistence the worst-case failure

decision: Reports never contain row values, only table, columns, row count
why: Exposed rows are likely third-party PII and reports land in CI logs

decision: No service-role key accepted in this task
why: Scan must see exactly what an outsider sees; avoids handling a secret

decision: Write probe: constraint-violation inference first, Prefer tx=rollback fallback, insert-then-delete forbidden
why: Owner chose A+B from the three options; C can leave rows in production when anon can insert but not delete

decision: Scope of first task confirmed: anon role, one live project, REST tables only
why: Owner confirmed restatement

decision: Rebased task/anon-probe onto origin/main (was cut from stale local main lacking harness setup)
why: Branch must start from current main

decision: Spiked RLS ordering in plain Postgres 16 instead of PostgREST
why: Docker Hub rate-limited (429); downloading the PostgREST binary was denied by the session's permission classifier; PostgREST facts P1-P4 left to the first ticket

decision: Method A confirmed sound for insert and update: WITH CHECK runs before constraints
why: 42501 vs 23502 observed for every policy shape tried

decision: Found two limits that conflict with the brief: pk-filling triggers let the probe row persist (S-4); value-based policies make blank-row rejection a false 'protected' (S-5)
why: Observed rows persisted (t_trig, t_trig2) and value policy accepted (t_owner)
evidence: spike2.sql A B E; design.md F6 F8

decision: Only write_probe may send mutating requests; report type has no field for row values
why: One owner for mutation and a structural guarantee for S-6

decision: Searched for public Supabase targets that invite attacks: found none live; closest is the self-hosted aceework11/supabase-rls-lab
why: Owner asked whether community test sites exist

decision: Two modes; first task is attack mode with real writes on a disposable copy, live probing moved to a later task; rlsentry positioned as research and teaching tool
why: Real writes mirror attacker behaviour and remove the F6/F8 conflicts; only disposable targets keep it safe

decision: A Lovable-generated app built as an inexperienced user would becomes a lab target
why: Realistic target for the research write-up shown to the professor

decision: Lovable target is attacked by replaying its migrations locally, not live; it is its own task
why: Keeps one safe code path; generating it needs the owner's Lovable account, which unattended work cannot use

decision: Attack-mode reports show one evidence row per finding
why: All rows are fake by construction; demonstrated evidence is the point of the tool

decision: Kept slug anon-probe despite the mode change
why: Renaming means deleting a pushed branch; the brief says it is attack mode

decision: brief-approved 0186693721f7e18bed2189e0d892dfb2df378af5
why: Owner said the brief is right; evidence rows in reports and a self-written lab confirmed

decision: Live-target guard is structural: attacker only accepts a channel the sandbox creates, plus a per-run nonce check
why: A skippable URL check is one bug away from attacking a real database

decision: Update/delete success confirmed through the superuser connection, not the REST response
why: RLS turns denied updates into 0-row successes

decision: Old live-probe design moved to live-probe-notes.md
why: Kept as evidence for roadmap task live-probe

decision: D-1 docker + local backends; D-2 attack via REST layer only; D-3 white-box value candidates allowed
why: Owner accepted the recommendations

decision: Tests run on the local backend; docker only when a daemon answers
why: No Docker daemon in the cloud image and Docker Hub returned 429

decision: Downloaded PostgREST v12.2.3 (sha256 9f71269e...) and verified it serves local PostgreSQL 16 with JSON error codes
why: Owner approved the download; the local backend needs it

decision: Session moved to cloud environment rlsentry-v2; setup script added installing shilaycow v0.4.2 skills and pinned PostgREST
why: Owner chose that environment; unattended runs need PostgREST; not yet proven on a freshly built container
